From Proto-Semitic *šim-, from Proto-Afroasiatic *sim- (“name”). Leveled in Arabic to the roots و س م (w s m) and س م و (s m w). Cognate with Hebrew שם (shém), Amharic ስም (sɨm).

parole.significato: to bear many children, to be prolific
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *baḳḳ- (“gnat”), ultimately stemming from Proto-Afroasiatic *ba(n)ḳ- (“troublesome insect”), with cognates in West Chadic, Fyer ḅakyáà-ŋ (“scorpion”), and to Cushitic, Hadiyya benḳ-aččo (“tick”). parole.significato: Used to form feminine adjectives from masculine adjectives.
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic *-at-, from Proto-Afroasiatic *-t, *-Vt (feminine suffix). See also Egyptian -t.
From Proto-Semitic *dubb- (“bear”), from Proto-Afroasiatic *dab- (“big animal”). Compare Aramaic דבא (debbā), Hebrew דוב (dov) and Akkadian dabûm.
From the root ذ ب ب (ḏ b b), from Proto-Semitic *ḏubab-, from Proto-Afroasiatic *ðuṗṗ. Cognate with Akkadian 𒉏 (zubbum) and Hebrew זְבוּב (zəbūb) and Amharic ዝምብ (zəmb).

From Proto-Semitic *riʔat- (“lung, breast, chest”), ultimately from Proto-Afroasiatic. Cognate with Hebrew רֵאָה (reʾá, “lung”), Classical Syriac ܪ̈ܲܐܘܵܬܵܐ (raˀṯā), Ugaritic 𐎛𐎗𐎚 (ỉrt), Akkadian 𒃮 (iratu), and Proto-Berber *t-irəʔ-t (“lung”) (whence Tashelhit turt (“lung”)).

Derived from the active participle of the verb رَعَى (raʕā, “to graze, to tend a flock”). From Proto-Semitic, from Proto-Afroasiatic *-raaʕ- (“to move along”). Cognate with Akkadian 𒉺𒇻 (rē'ûm) and Biblical Hebrew רֹעֶה (roʿɛ).

Ultimately from Proto-Semitic *ʕall-, *ʕaly- (“to be high; exalted”), from Proto-Afroasiatic *ʕal-, *ʕVl(ay)- (“to be high, tall; to rise, ascend”). Cognate with Hebrew עָלָה (ʿalá, “to ascend, rise, grow, develop”), Hebrew עלי (ʿeli, “ascent”) and thereby Eli.

From the root ع ن ب (ʕ n b), from Proto-Semitic *ʿanbab- (“fruit, flower, shoot”), ultimately Proto-Afroasiatic *ʿanbab- (“plant, flower”). Inherited from Proto-Semitic *ʕayn-, from Proto-Afroasiatic *ʕayVn-.

parole.significato: the back of the neck, the nape
parole.testo: From the root ق ف و (q f w). From Proto-Semitic *ḳapy- (“back of the head”), from Proto-Afroasiatic *ḳapay- (“back of the head”).
From Proto-Semitic *qayθ̣- (“summer”), from Proto-Afroasiatic *ḳayč̣- (“to be hot; summer”). Cognate with Aramaic קֵיטָא (qēṭā) and Hebrew קַיִץ (káyits, qáyiṣ).
Inherited from Proto-Semitic *libb- (“heart”), from Proto-Afroasiatic *lib-. Cognate with Hebrew לב (lev) and Classical Syriac ܠܒܐ (lebbā).

Inherited from Proto-Semitic *laḥm- (“food, eatables; meat, bread”), from Proto-Afroasiatic *laḥam- (“food”). Cognate with Aramaic לַחְמָא (laḥmā), Classical Syriac ܠܚܡܐ (laḥmā), Hebrew לֶחֶם (léḥem), Ugaritic 𐎍𐎈𐎎 (lḥm /⁠laḥmu⁠/), Ge'ez ላህም (lahm), all meaning “food” or “bread”. The varying semantic
From Proto-Semitic *lawn, from Proto-Afroasiatic *lwn-; cognate with Egyptian jwn.

parole.significato: a prefix used to create nouns of place
parole.testo: From Proto-Semitic, from Proto-Afroasiatic *m-. Cognate with Proto-Berber *-m- and Egyptian m-. Sometimes thought to be derived from the pronouns present in Arabic مَا (mā), Hebrew מה (mā, “what”), and مَن (man), מי (mī, “who”), so that, for example, مُدَرِّس (mudarris, “teacher”) is originally من ي

From Proto-Semitic *mahir-/*marw- (“(young) man; still fast and physically useful”), possibly further Proto-Afroasiatic *ma(hi)r- (“servant, slave”), potentially related to Arabic مَرْء (marʔ). Compare Akkadian 𒌉 (mārum, “young man, son; subordinate, deployable man, service man, usable worker, hirel
Inherited from Proto-Semitic *nayak-, outside of Arabia only attested by Akkadian 𒈾𒀀𒆪 (nâku). Ultimately from Proto-Afroasiatic; compare Egyptian n:k-D53 (nk).

From Proto-Semitic *waqar- (“to be heavy or weighty; a tree laden with fruits; to be honorable or to hold weight in value”), from Proto-Afroasiatic *waqar-; compare Egyptian jqr (“excellent, worthy”) and Hebrew יָקָר (“expensive, dear, precious”).
Inherited from Proto-Semitic *-ī and/or Proto-Semitic *-ya, from Proto-Afroasiatic *yi (“me”). Compare Biblical Hebrew ־ִי (-i).

parole.significato: The nisba suffix, an extremely productive suffix used to derive adjectives (with the meaning “related to ...”) or nouns…
parole.testo: Compare Akkadian -ī, Biblical Hebrew ־ִי (-i) and Egyptian -j.
From Proto-Semitic *yamīn- (“right”), from Proto-Afroasiatic *yamin- (“right”).
